purpose: Integrates WP 6.7+ native WebP/AVIF support with format downgrade detection, adds native lazy loading toggle with JS/HTML integration, loading optimization attributes via wp_get_loading_optimization_attributes(), cache group flushing, WP 6.9+ cache salt support in Redis drop-in, and fixes multiple critical bugs from prior review iterations (Delay JS broken, AVIF hook skipped, excluded image attributes lost).
riskRationale: All previously reported critical/important issues (Delay JS broken, AVIF hook skipped, excluded images losing forced attributes) are confirmed fixed. Two new integration gaps were introduced: replace_image_with_next_gen() reads raw options instead of the downgraded format (causing unnecessary WebP queue entries), and the 'skipped' conversion status isn't cleaned from pending. These do not break visible functionality but waste Action Scheduler resources and may show stale unconverted entries to the user.

text: All 6 previously reported critical/important issues from prior iterations are confirmed fixed (Delay JS registration, AVIF conversion hooks, excluded image attributes, convert_image 'both' guard, dead function_exists guard, lazy observer creation). The PR correctly handles WP 6.7+ format downgrade in the converter class, hook registration, and loading optimization attributes. Two new integration gaps were found in the inline image serving path and conversion status handler, both causing unnecessary queue churn on WP 6.7+ when core handles WebP. Two additional minor code quality findings across lazyload.js and object-cache.php round out the review.

reasoning: One important issue (replace_image_with_next_gen reading raw options instead of downgraded format) and three minor issues remain. All are straightforward 1-5 line fixes with no risk of regression. No visible functionality is broken on any supported WP version.

message: replace_image_with_next_gen() reads raw $conversionFormat option value instead of using the downgraded format from Img_Converter::get_format(). On WP 6.7+ when core handles WebP natively and user selected 'webp', the format is downgraded to 'none' internally, but this method still sees 'webp'. It queues WebP conversion on every page load — conversions that will be silently skipped by the convert_image() guard. This creates persistent 'pending' queue entries that never resolve and wastes Action Scheduler resources if the user triggers bulk conversion.
suggestion: Use the converter's get_format() method which reflects the format downgrade. Add $img_converter = $this->get_img_converter() before the $conversion_format assignment, then change to $conversion_format = $img_converter->get_format(). This ensures the downgraded format is used for conversion decisions.

message: update_conversion_status() does not handle the 'skipped' status for pending removal. The 'completed' and 'failed' statuses both remove the image from the 'pending' list, but 'skipped' (newly introduced by this PR's guard in convert_image()) does not. This means images that are skipped (WebP when core handles it) remain in the 'pending' queue indefinitely. While add_img_into_queue() prevents duplicates, the pending entries persist and may be displayed to the user as unconverted.
suggestion: Add a 'skipped' status handler in update_conversion_status that removes the image from pending, mirroring the existing 'failed' handler.

message: Hardcoded selector 'video.wppo-lazy-video' instead of using the LAZY_SELECTOR constant. Functionally identical since LAZY_SELECTOR in native mode resolves to the same string, but using the constant improves maintainability and consistency with querySelectorAll calls elsewhere in the file.
suggestion: Replace the hardcoded string 'video.wppo-lazy-video' with the LAZY_SELECTOR constant.

message: The method_exists($wp_object_cache, 'add_salt') check is redundant when the preceding instanceof WP_Object_Cache check already guarantees the method exists. Adds unnecessary cognitive overhead.
suggestion: Remove the method_exists check since instanceof already confirms the class has the method.

message: Undefined variable $keys in set_multiple() error path. When the Redis pipeline fails (returns non-array), the code references $keys which is not defined in this scope. The parameter name is $data, not $keys (delete_multiple uses $keys as its parameter name, but this is set_multiple). This triggers a PHP notice and returns array_fill(0, 0, false) = [] instead of an error-indicating array matching the input size.
suggestion: Replace $keys with $data on line 408 to reference the correct parameter variable.

message: The flush_group() method is well-designed with a proper function_exists guard, enabling targeted cache flushing instead of full cache clears.

set_loading_optimization_attributes() cleanly separates core wp_get_loading_optimization_attributes() usage from fallback defaults, with correct attribute presence checks to avoid overwriting existing values, and applies fallback attributes outside the if/else branch ensuring excluded images always receive forced fetchpriority and decoding on all WP versions.

Delay JS filter is unconditionally registered when the option is active, completely independent of the defer strategy — correctly separating two distinct concerns and fixing the silent non-functional delay JS feature.
add_defer_strategy correctly uses wp_script_add_data with 'strategy' => 'defer' for WP 6.7+, which is cleaner than regex-based defer injection.

The AVIF hook condition was correctly changed from format-specific exclusion to 'none' !== get_format(), fixing the AVIF conversion regression on WP 6.7+ while correctly skipping the hook only when core handles all formats natively.
The convert_image skip guard correctly uses in_array() to check both 'webp' and 'both' formats via format(), preventing redundant WebP conversion when core handles it natively.
Elegant early-return guard avoids creating IntersectionObserver, MutationObserver on document.body, and periodic safety scan intervals when native lazy is active and no video elements are present.
